gloss: main enclosure of a castle; castle keep area

definitions.gloss: main enclosure of a castle; castle keep area
definitions.explanation: The innermost and most heavily fortified area of a Japanese castle, containing the main tower and lord's residence.

definitions.gloss: main target; the heart of the matter; central stronghold
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, the most important or central part of something; the real target or core issue.

{本丸|ほんまる}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{石垣|いしがき}→石垣：19673_ishigaki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{高|たか}くて→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦{立派|りっぱ}→立派：01093_rippa⟧だ。

notes:
{本|ほん} (main, true) + ⟦{丸|まる}→丸：02167_maru⟧ (enclosure, bailey). Originally a castle architecture term, now widely used figuratively in politics and journalism.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {本丸|ほんまる}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{切|き}り{込|こ}む: get to the heart of the matter
- {本丸|ほんまる}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{迫|せま}る→迫る：03928_semaru⟧: close in on the main target
- ⟦{改革|かいかく}→改革：04815_kaikaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{本丸|ほんまる}: the core of reform
- {本丸|ほんまる}⟦{御殿|ごてん}→御殿：24076_goten⟧: main enclosure palace

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {二|に}の{丸|まる}: second enclosure — the area surrounding the main enclosure
- {三|さん}の{丸|まる}: third enclosure — the outermost bailey
- ⟦{核心|かくしん}→核心：13105_kakushin⟧: core, crux — a more general word for the central point of an issue

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese castles were built with concentric defensive rings. The {本丸|ほんまる} was the last line of defense, containing the lord's quarters and the ⟦{天守閣|てんしゅかく}→天守閣：17449_tenshukaku⟧ (castle tower). The figurative use — meaning the real target or the most important objective — is especially common in political reporting.
